item.title: Speak Easy, Move Loud – Continuum and Resilience
item.description: Resilience Dance Company and Continuum Vocal Ensemble will present “Speak Easy | Move Loud” on February 6 and 7. Emily Haussler, Artistic and Executive Director of RDC, and Dr. John McDonald, Artistic Director of Continuum, tell listeners about this event that explores ideas of resistance, cultural upheaval, identity and belonging through music and movement. item.description: Saint Louis Women’s Chorale Artistic and Executive Director Leanne Magnuson Latuda and Kathy Lawton Brown dive into the world of Imaginary Creatures and the magic that has gone into creating this mystical performance. Step into an enchanted realm with the Saint Louis Women’s Chorale on February 15, 2026, at the Center of Creative Arts (COCA) as music and dance conjure a dazzling tapestry of myth and wonder. item.description: Violist Michael Casimir and cellist Yin Xiong, co-curators of Songs of Belonging, the February 5th SLSO Live at The Sheldon concert, share how the program came together, which pieces are their personal favorites, and why the theme seems especially important right now. item.title: Kingsbury Gallery ART TALK with Richard Cummings
item.description: Kingsbury Gallery – at Grace and Peace Fellowship Curator and Director Nancy Hughes and Dr. Richard Cummings, professor of art at College of the Ozarks, join Kathy Lawton Brown for a conversation about “Art Talk” on February 15, 2026. We’ll also hear about the exhibit CLAY. WHAT WE MAKE OF IT with works from eight ceramicists running through March 22. Learn more with Kingsbury Gallery – at Grace and Peace Fellowship on Facebook. item.title: Melissa Dunphy on Suite Justice Premiere
item.description: We look forward to welcoming composer Melissa Dunphy for “Friday Morning with the Arts” at 9am on February 13, 2026. We’ll talk about her world premiere piece, part of the Saint Louis Chamber Chorus concert “Justice: From Abraham Lincoln to MLK” happening on Sunday, February 15. This piece was commissioned for The Saint Louis Chamber Chorus by the family of Suzanne Haubein in honor of her wonderful music-making. item.title: Tom Sudholt Celebrates 40 Years
item.description: A message from Julie Schuster: This month marks a special anniversary for one of our hosts at Classic 107.3. Tom Sudholt is celebrating 40 years in radio broadcasting! item.title: In Harmony with The St. Louis Children’s Choirs
item.description: Ben Nordstrom, Executive Director for The Saint Louis Children’s Choirs (SLCC), talks with Kathy Lawton Brown about current and upcoming events. Listen to learn about rolling auditions that now underway for students in grades 3-12. Students currently in 1st or 2nd grade are welcome to audition for placement for the 2026-2027 season starting February 25th, 2026. item.title: Art in Bloom Celebrates 20 Years
item.description: Amanda Thompson Rundahl, the Director of Learning and Engagement for the Saint Louis Art Museum, tells listeners about the history of Art in Bloom, which is happening February 27-March 1. Hear about how art works and floral artists are selected, and learn about some of the special events associated with the 20th Art in Bloom at SLAM. item.title: St. Louis Symphony Preview: Bernstein and Robertson
item.description: Co-hosts Tom Sudholt and Chuck Lavazzi discuss the St. Louis Symphony Orchestra‘s program for this weekend. Bernstein and Robertson — American Reflections with performances on March 6–7. David Robertson, SLSO Music Director from 2005 to 2018, returns to conduct a compelling program exploring evolution and change through works by four American musical luminaries.
